rubrics.justification: The response gives a plausible expanded blastocyst assessment with reasonable ICM/TE grading, but it includes some potentially overconfident image-specific details (e.g., exact ICM location, cavity debris/granularity, zona thinning) that may not be reliably supported from a single image.
It integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, prior live births, endometrium, sperm data, and lifestyle factors well, and connects them to prognosis, though some links are somewhat speculative.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with a clear logic from morphology and patient factors to prognosis; minor issues include speculative quantitative adjustments and some unsupported assumptions.

Much of the advice is broadly evidence-based (SET, smoking/alcohol counseling, standard luteal support), but recommendations such as adding estradiol for a thick endometrium, ERA after a single failure, broad thrombophilia screening, and routine PGT-A implication in a 31-year-old are not strongly guideline-supported.

The recommendations are clear and practical for both the current transfer and future planning, including lifestyle modification and possible protocol review, though a few suggestions are more aggressive than standard practice.
